summary: Tested the live single-location API and desktop/mobile UI. Core navigation, searchable movements, catalog controls, history editing UI, multi-item controls, and dealer profile work; posted movement edit recalculates available stock but corrupts inward/outward totals.

critical.issue: Editing a posted inward movement reverses available stock but increments the inward counter instead of decrementing it. A 7-unit inward corrected to 4 left available=4 but inward increased to 18. The same direction-sign bug affects outward counters and kind changes.

issues: At 390px the 238px sidebar remains visible and the main content is squeezed/clipped into the remaining width; navigation/content is not practically usable despite document scrollWidth being hidden to the viewport.

action_items: Fix reverse_transaction/stock_change so reversing a posted movement decrements the original inward/outward counters, then apply the corrected movement; verify edits that change inward to outward too.
Add a mobile navigation/layout treatment (collapse or hide the sidebar and give main content full width) rather than relying on overflow-x hidden.
critical_code_review_comments: stock_change applies inward/outward counter increments independent of direction, so reverse_transaction is not mathematically inverse and audit edits silently corrupt aggregate stock metrics.

success_rate.backend: 50% (1/2 focused tests; edit recalculation failed counter assertion)
success_rate.frontend: 100% exercised flows; mobile usability issue found

seed_data_creation: Focused API test created TEST-prefixed brand, battery, and inward movement, then edited that movement. Existing preview database also contains prior TEST/UI regression records. No APIs were mocked.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Warehouse removal is reflected: bootstrap omits warehouses and all stock rows use main-stock. Supplier/dealer/battery typeahead, brand quick-add control, multi-item line controls, history edit modal, catalog, stock-out search, and dealer profile were exercised successfully. Re-run the focused test after fixing counter reversal, and test mobile navigation usability.
rca of the issue: In server.py, stock_change computes available delta using direction but increments inward/outward using only kind. reverse_transaction therefore subtracts available while adding to the original movement counter; applying the edited movement adds counters again. This leaves available apparently correct but aggregate inward/outward totals wrong.
